title: Church Hurt and Christ’s Faithfulness
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Church hurt and Christ’s faithfulness teaches that sins, failures, hypocrisy, or wounds caused by church people do not cancel the love, truth, or care of Christ for His sheep. Christ remains faithful even when His people fail.
summary: Church hurt and Christ’s faithfulness teaches that sins, failures, hypocrisy, or wounds caused by church people do not cancel the love, truth, or care of Christ for His sheep. Christ remains faithful even when His people fail.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the faithful Shepherd of His church. He sees wounded sheep, judges sin, corrects His people, and continues to love and care for those hurt by human failure.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Church hurt is real. People may be wounded by hypocrisy, harsh leadership, neglect, gossip, abuse, manipulation, false teaching, favoritism, or failure to protect the vulnerable.

Scripture does not pretend God’s people never fail. The Bible contains warnings to shepherds, corrections to churches, and commands to protect the flock. Christ takes the care of His sheep seriously.

Human failure does not cancel Christ’s faithfulness. The church belongs to Him, and He remains the Good Shepherd even when under-shepherds fail. Wounded believers must not be told to ignore pain, but they should be pointed back to Christ.

Healing from church hurt may require truth, repentance, accountability, wise boundaries, patient care, and time. Christ can restore trust without requiring denial of what happened.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people leave wounded by churches and assume Christ Himself has rejected them. This doctrine separates the failure of people from the faithfulness of the Savior.

It also calls churches to repentance. Christ’s name must not be used to cover harm. He loves His sheep and holds His church accountable to His Word.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring church wounds honestly to Christ. Do not confuse sinful people with the Savior who loves you. Seek wise, safe, biblical counsel, and ask God to restore your hope without forcing denial. If you serve in ministry, treat Christ’s sheep with holy care.
